title: How dynamic is the heavy metals pollution in the Buriganga River of Bangladesh? A spatiotemporal assessment based on environmental indices
authors: N. Majed, M. I. H. Real, A. Redwan, H. M. Azam
venue: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
abstract: Frequent discharge of heavy metals from textiles, tanneries and other anthropogenic sources occurs in Dhaka City, contaminating major rivers. Accumulation of heavy metals (Cr, Cd, Pb, Ni, Zn) in water, sediment, phytoplankton and fish species was investigated in Buriganga River at three distinct discharge points (Basila Bridge, Hazaribagh, Babu Bazar). Chromium (Cr) was found at alarming levels (103 mg/kg in soil, 163 mg/kg in plants) near the Hazaribagh tannery waste discharge point. Biological samples showed clear evidence of bioaccumulation. This study emphasizes the necessity of controlling point and nonpoint urban pollution sources.
